input: Replace the worn-out running shoes this week

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing what type of running the shoes are for (road, trail, track, treadmill) completely changes which shoe models and features are relevant.
Whether the shoes are for the user themselves or as a gift for someone else changes who needs to be involved in fitting, sizing, and preference decisions.
Budget is a hard limit that narrows the field dramatically — entry-level shoes start around $60 while performance models can exceed $250.
Whether the user plans to shop in-store or online affects the immediate next steps — in-store allows fitting and gait analysis, online requires knowing size and specs in advance.
Specific needs like arch support, cushioning level, or a preferred brand will steer the recommendation toward a much shorter list of options.
Knowing whether they already have a shortlist of shoes or are starting from scratch determines whether the first step is research or going straight to purchase.
Understanding what went wrong with the current shoes (too little cushioning, wrong fit, durability issues) defines what 'done well' looks like for the replacement.

gold.taskTitle: Replace worn-out running shoes this week
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to buy a new pair of running shoes to replace their current worn-out pair within this week.

questions.title: What surface or terrain do you mainly run on?
questions.description: Determines the shoe category needed — road, trail, track, or treadmill — which is the single biggest filter when choosing a model.

questions.title: Are you buying these for yourself or someone else?
questions.description: Establishes who needs to be involved in sizing, fitting, and preference decisions throughout the process.

questions.title: What is your budget for this purchase?
questions.description: A hard financial limit that immediately narrows the pool of viable shoe options.

questions.title: Do you plan to shop in-store or buy online?
questions.description: Dictates the entire action path — in-store enables gait analysis and fitting, while online requires upfront research into size and specs.

questions.title: Do you have any fit or support preferences, like cushioning level?
questions.description: Specific preferences such as arch support type, heel drop, or cushioning thickness steer recommendations toward a much shorter list.

questions.title: Do you already have specific models in mind to consider?
questions.description: Determines whether the first step is broad research or skipping straight to comparison and purchase of a known shortlist.

questions.title: What was the main problem with your current shoes?
questions.description: Identifies the failure point of the old pair — poor cushioning, wrong fit, durability — which defines what success looks like for the replacement.
